events.title: Devlog: the anomaly almost nobody found
events.summary: Before the demo came out, one of its anomalies was a door handle that had been flipped the wrong way round. We thought it was fair. You disagreed: only 8% of players spotted it the first time, and most never did. So on 10 October we replaced it with a fire hose in the maintenance room. That turned out to be nearly as hard. events.title: Coming from Backrooms Anomaly? Here's what's different in Pools
events.summary: If you played Backrooms Anomaly, you already know the rule: look for anything that's off, turn back if something changed, keep going if nothing did. Pools keeps that rule and moves it somewhere much wetter. The poolrooms. Tiled corridors, flooded chambers and empty pools instead of yellow wallpaper and carpet. Two stages. events.title: 755 players. What got you?
events.summary: Thanks to everyone who has gone into the poolrooms since the demo came out on 16 October. 755 of you have played so far, and between you you've made just over 16,000 calls. We went through the numbers to see which anomalies people walk straight past. The easy ones Almost everyone spots the giant statue head on the first try (90%), and the colourful slides aren't far behind (88%). Fair enough. They're not subtle. events.title: Our new game Backrooms Anomaly launches July 24
events.summary: Hey everyone! Backrooms Anomaly: Pools is the sequel to Backrooms Anomaly, so this is the best place to start. Backrooms Anomaly launches July 24 with a 30% launch discount. If you're interested in Pools, wishlist this one now so you get notified when it goes live. It's a horror game about hunting anomalies.
